name: Open Sub Account
description: open a sub-account for member {member_id} in branch {branch_code} with an initial deposit of {initial_deposit}, leaving the account type at its default, then read the new account number

outputs.name: new_account_number
outputs.description: Value read from cell 'New Account Number'.

steps.description: Open open sub account at the entry URL.
The Member ID field is the first required input to locate member {member_id}.

target.robustness_note: Identifying the textbox 'Member ID'. 5 rung(s) verified against the live surface at record time. Rung 1 — role+name: the control exposes the accessible name 'Member ID', which survives restyling and DOM churn. Rung 1 — name alone: 'Member ID' identifies it without relying on the role the tree assigns. Rung 2 — relational: the textbox sharing a row with the caption 'Member ID' (occurrence 1). Rung 3 — structural: the textbox at position 0 in reading order, which breaks if a control is inserted before it. Rung 4 — coordinates: last resort, viewport-bound, and the only rung that would still work on a surface with no queryable tree at all.

known_outcomes.name: sub_account_opened
known_outcomes.message: The sub-account was created and its number read.

known_outcomes.name: approval_limit_exceeded
known_outcomes.message: The deposit exceeds this operator's approval limit. A real answer: the bank declined, and a human with a higher limit must finish it.

known_outcomes.name: member_not_found
known_outcomes.message: No member exists with that ID, so there is nothing to open a sub-account against.

known_outcomes.name: permission_denied
known_outcomes.message: The operating account may not view this member.

known_outcomes.name: invalid_deposit
known_outcomes.message: The app rejected the deposit as unparseable, so our type step sent something wrong. Our bug.
